content.title: About
content.content: A pumpernickel roll is a small, round bun made from whole‑grain rye flour. It has a dense, slightly tangy crust and a soft, aromatic crumb. Pumpernickel rolls are often used as a base for sandwiches, appetizers, or as a side for soups and salads.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Pumpernickel bread is a traditional staple in Scandinavian and Eastern European cuisines.
Its dark color comes from the use of malt and caramel, not artificial coloring.
Rye flour provides more fiber and minerals than wheat flour, making the roll more nutritious.
In some regions the rolls are baked with caraway or coriander seeds for extra flavor.
Pumpernickel rolls are a common component of the classic Swedish open‑face sandwich (smörgås).

items.title: High in fiber
items.content: Rye flour contains both soluble and insoluble fiber, which supports digestive health.

items.title: Low glycemic index
items.content: Compared with white bread, pumpernickel rolls raise blood sugar more slowly, beneficial for glucose control.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: The roll provides thiamine, niacin, and folate, essential for energy metabolism.

items.title: Contains minerals
items.content: It supplies magnesium, iron, and zinc, supporting muscle function and immunity.

items.title: Promotes satiety
items.content: Complex carbs and fiber help you feel full longer.

items.title: Grain allergy
items.content: People allergic to wheat or other grains may react to pumpernickel rolls.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Some recipes add salt, so those monitoring sodium should check the label.

items.title: Gluten
items.content: Pumpernickel rolls contain gluten and are not suitable for individuals with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Pumpernickel rolls are perfect for sandwiches with fish, ham, or vegetables, sliced in half and spread with butter or cream cheese. They also make a hearty side for soups, stews, or as a base for open‑face appetizers.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep rolls in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 2‑3 days. For longer storage, refrigerate (up to a week) or freeze (up to 3 months). Discard any rolls that show mold or a stale, sour smell.
